sentence: 'I'm exhausted,' she said. She said she ___ exhausted.
explanation: Present simple/progressive shifts to past in reported speech: am → was.

sentence: 'I work from home on Fridays,' he explained. He explained that he ___ from home on Fridays.
explanation: After a past reporting verb, present simple backshifts to past simple: work → worked.

sentence: 'We're moving to Lisbon,' they announced. They announced that they ___ to Lisbon.
explanation: Present continuous backshifts to past continuous: are moving → were moving.

sentence: 'I've lost my keys,' she admitted. She admitted that she ___ her keys.
explanation: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect: have lost → had lost.

sentence: 'I saw the accident happen,' the witness stated. The witness stated that he ___ the accident happen.
explanation: Past simple backshifts to past perfect after a past reporting verb: saw → had seen.

sentence: 'The train left ten minutes ago,' she said. She said the train ___ ten minutes before.
explanation: Past simple becomes past perfect, and 'ago' becomes 'before': had left ten minutes before.

sentence: 'I'll call you later,' he promised. He promised that he ___ call me later.
explanation: Will backshifts to would in reported speech.

sentence: 'We won't stay long,' they said. They said they ___ stay long.
explanation: will not → would not (wouldn't) after a past reporting verb.

sentence: 'I can swim,' the boy boasted. The boy boasted that he ___ swim.
explanation: Can backshifts to could in reported speech.

sentence: 'You may leave early,' the manager said. The manager said we ___ leave early.
explanation: May (permission/possibility) backshifts to might.

sentence: 'I must finish this today,' she said. She said she ___ finish it that day.
explanation: Must expressing obligation usually becomes had to in reported speech; 'today' becomes 'that day'.

sentence: 'I'll be waiting outside the cinema,' he said. He said he ___ waiting outside the cinema.
explanation: will be + -ing becomes would be + -ing in reported speech.

sentence: 'I've been studying all night,' she said. She said she ___ studying all night.
hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
explanation: have been + -ing backshifts to had been + -ing.

sentence: 'They were arguing all through dinner,' he said. He said they ___ arguing all through dinner.
explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: were arguing → had been arguing.

sentence: 'I had already eaten,' she said. She said she ___ already eaten.
explanation: The past perfect cannot backshift further; it remains had + past participle.

sentence: 'The shop closes at six,' she reminded me. She reminded me that the shop ___ at six.
explanation: Even habitual present simple backshifts after a past reporting verb: closes → closed.

sentence: 'I don't like seafood,' he confessed. He confessed that he ___ like seafood.
explanation: Present simple negative backshifts: don't like → didn't like.

sentence: 'We may be a few minutes late,' they warned. They warned that they ___ be a few minutes late.
explanation: May (possibility) backshifts to might after 'warned'.

sentence: 'I have to catch the last train,' she said. She said she ___ catch the last train.
explanation: Have to (obligation) backshifts to had to after a past reporting verb.

sentence: 'I might take a gap year,' he said. He said he ___ take a gap year.
explanation: Might has no further backshift form; it stays might.

sentence: 'I can't find my passport anywhere,' she moaned. She moaned that she ___ find her passport anywhere.
explanation: Negative can backshifts to couldn't in reported speech.

sentence: 'We've been waiting for hours,' the passengers complained. The passengers complained that they ___ waiting for hours.
hint: present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous
explanation: have been waiting → had been waiting after the past reporting verb 'complained'.

sentence: 'I will always love you,' he whispered. He whispered that he ___ always love me.
explanation: Will backshifts to would; 'you' shifts to 'me' from the speaker's new perspective.

sentence: 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher said. The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
explanation: Timeless general truths may keep the present simple after a past reporting verb.

sentence: 'I was living in Berlin at the time,' she recalled. She recalled that she ___ living in Berlin at the time.
explanation: Past continuous backshifts to past perfect continuous: was living → had been living.

sentence: 'I'd love to come,' she said. She said she ___ love to come.
explanation: 'I'd love' is I would love; would does not change in reported speech.

sentence: 'We'd already booked when you called,' they said. They said they ___ already booked when I called.
explanation: Past perfect stays past perfect; only the pronoun you → I shifts.

sentence: 'I'm about to leave,' he said at six. At six he said he ___ about to leave.
explanation: 'Be about to' backshifts like any present form: am about to → was about to.

sentence: 'You can rely on me,' she assured me. She assured me that I ___ rely on her.
explanation: Can backshifts to could after the past reporting verb 'assured'.

sentence: 'The road is being resurfaced,' the council said. The council said the road ___ resurfaced.
explanation: Present continuous passive (is being resurfaced) backshifts to past continuous passive: was being resurfaced.

sentence: 'Someone has stolen my bike,' he cried. He cried that someone ___ his bike.
explanation: have stolen backshifts to had stolen after the past reporting verb 'cried'.

sentence: 'I'll have finished by noon,' she promised. She promised she ___ finished by noon.
explanation: will have + past participle becomes would have + past participle.

sentence: 'We might have missed the turning,' he admitted. He admitted that they ___ have missed the turning.
explanation: Might has no further backshift form, so it is unchanged.

sentence: 'I used to live in Cairo,' she mentioned. She mentioned that she ___ to live in Cairo.
explanation: 'Used to' has no backshift form; it remains used to after a past reporting verb.

sentence: 'You must be joking!' I exclaimed. I exclaimed that he ___ be joking.
hint: must of deduction does not backshift
explanation: Must expressing confident deduction usually stays must; only obligation shifts to had to.

sentence: 'Where do you live?' he asked me. He asked me where I ___.
explanation: Reported questions use statement word order, and present simple backshifts: do you live → I lived.

sentence: 'What time does the bank open?' she asked. She asked what time the bank ___.
explanation: The question reverts to statement word order and the verb backshifts: opens → opened.

sentence: 'Are you coming to the party?' they asked me. They asked ___ coming to the party.
explanation: Yes/no questions become if/whether clauses; pronouns and tenses shift: if I was coming.

sentence: 'Have you finished the report?' the boss asked. The boss asked ___ finished the report.
hint: present perfect → past perfect in a yes/no question
explanation: Have you finished → whether/if I had finished; statement word order throughout.

sentence: 'Why did you cancel the order?' he asked. He asked why I ___ the order.
explanation: Wh-questions keep the wh-word but drop do-support and backshift: did you cancel → I had cancelled.

sentence: 'How long have you worked here?' she asked him. She asked him how long he ___ there.
explanation: have worked → had worked; 'here' becomes 'there' in reported speech.

sentence: 'Do you speak Japanese?' the interviewer asked. The interviewer asked ___ Japanese.
explanation: Yes/no question → if I spoke; present simple backshifts to past simple.

sentence: 'Where are you going?' she asked her brother. She asked her brother where he ___ going.
explanation: are you going → he was going: statement order with backshifted continuous.

sentence: 'Who broke the window?' the teacher demanded. The teacher demanded ___ the window.
explanation: 'Demand to know + wh-clause' with statement order; past simple backshifts to past perfect.

sentence: 'Will you marry me?' he asked her. He asked her ___ marry him.
explanation: Will you...? → if/whether she would...: statement word order, backshifted modal.

sentence: 'When did the ancient city fall?' we asked the guide. We asked the guide when the ancient city ___.
explanation: did...fall → had fallen: the auxiliary 'did' disappears and the verb backshifts.

sentence: 'Which seat do you prefer?' the steward asked. The steward asked which seat I ___.
explanation: do you prefer → I preferred: statement order, present simple backshifted.

sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

sentence: 'Shall I close the window?' he asked. He asked ___ close the window.
explanation: Shall I...? (offering) becomes if/whether he should... in reported speech.

sentence: 'Have you ever been to Iceland?' she asked. She asked ___ ever been to Iceland.
explanation: Have you been → if I had been: if/whether with past perfect.

sentence: 'What are your plans for the weekend?' he asked. He asked what my plans for the weekend ___.
explanation: are → were: the copula backshifts like any other verb.

sentence: 'Where will you be staying?' they asked. They asked where ___ be staying.
hint: future continuous backshift in a question
explanation: will you be staying → I would be staying: statement order, would for will.

sentence: 'Do you know the way?' she asked me. She asked me ___ the way.
explanation: Do you know → if I knew: no do-support in the reported clause.

sentence: 'How much does this cost?' I asked the vendor. I asked the vendor how much it ___.
explanation: does cost → cost: the past simple of 'cost' is 'cost', used with statement word order.

sentence: 'Do you take sugar?' he asked. He asked ___ took sugar.
explanation: Yes/no questions take if/whether, not do-support or 'that': asked if I took sugar.

sentence: 'Sit down, please,' the nurse said to me. The nurse asked me ___ down.
explanation: Requests are reported with ask + object + to-infinitive: asked me to sit down.

sentence: 'Don't touch the wet paint,' the caretaker warned us. The caretaker warned us ___ the wet paint.
explanation: Negative commands become not to + infinitive after told/asked/warned.

sentence: 'Leave the building immediately!' the firefighter ordered. The firefighter ordered us ___ the building immediately.
explanation: Orders are reported with order + object + to-infinitive.

sentence: 'Please, please help me,' the woman begged. The woman begged ___ her.
explanation: Begging is reported as beg + somebody + to do something.

sentence: 'Don't forget to lock up,' my mother said. My mother reminded me ___ up.
explanation: 'Don't forget' corresponds to remind + object + to-infinitive.

sentence: 'Stop the car!' the passenger shouted. The passenger shouted at the driver ___ the car.
hint: shout at sb to do sth
explanation: The command is reported with shout at + object + to-infinitive.

sentence: 'Don't be late again,' the coach told him. The coach told him ___ late again.
explanation: Negative commands: not to be, with the negative before the whole infinitive.

sentence: 'Could you open the window?' she asked. She asked me ___ the window.
explanation: 'Could you...?' requests are reported with ask + object + to-infinitive; no could remains.

sentence: 'Get out of my way!' the guard snapped. The guard snapped at me ___ out of my way.
hint: snap at sb to do sth
explanation: The order is reported as snapped at me + to-infinitive.

sentence: 'Please don't smoke in here,' the host said. The host asked me ___ in there.
explanation: Negative requests: asked me not to smoke; 'here' shifts to 'there'.

sentence: 'Hand in your phones,' the invigilator instructed. The invigilator instructed us ___ in our phones.
explanation: Formal commands: instruct + object + to-infinitive; the particle 'in' stays with the verb.

sentence: 'Please reconsider my application,' she wrote. She ___ them to reconsider her application.
explanation: A polite written request is reported with asked + object + to-infinitive.

sentence: 'Don't leave your belongings unattended,' the announcement repeated. The announcement ___ passengers not to leave their belongings unattended.
hint: warn sb not to do sth
explanation: The warning fits warn + object + not to + infinitive.

sentence: 'Please, please don't leave me,' he sobbed. He begged her ___ leave him.
hint: beg sb not to do sth
explanation: Negative begging: begged her not to leave; the negative precedes the infinitive.

sentence: 'I'll see you tomorrow,' he said. He said he would see me ___.
explanation: Time expressions shift: tomorrow becomes the next day / the following day.

sentence: 'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.

sentence: 'We're leaving here at dawn,' they said. They said they were leaving ___ at dawn.
explanation: Place adverbs shift with the speaker's perspective: here → there.

sentence: 'I'll finish the report today,' she said. She said she would finish the report ___.
explanation: Today becomes that day when reported later.

sentence: 'I moved here two years ago,' he explained. He explained that he had moved there two years ___.
explanation: 'Ago' becomes 'before' (or 'earlier') in reported speech; here → there as well.

sentence: 'I'm meeting them tomorrow evening,' she said. She said she was meeting them ___ evening.
explanation: Tomorrow evening becomes the next (or the following) evening.

sentence: 'We stayed at this hotel last summer,' they recalled. They recalled that they had stayed at ___ hotel the summer before.
explanation: Demonstratives shift: this hotel → that hotel; last summer → the summer before.

sentence: 'The flight leaves now,' the announcer said. The announcer said that the flight left ___.
explanation: Now becomes then in reported speech.

sentence: 'I'll call you next week,' he promised. He promised he would call me ___.
explanation: 'Next week' shifts to the following week (or the next week) from a later standpoint.

sentence: 'She arrived last night,' he told us. He told us that she had arrived ___.
explanation: 'Last night' becomes the night before (the previous night) in reported speech.

sentence: 'I saw him this morning,' she said on Monday afternoon. She said she had seen him ___ morning.
explanation: This morning, reported later the same day, becomes that morning.

sentence: 'Come round to my house tomorrow,' she said. She invited me round to her house ___.
explanation: Tomorrow becomes the next day (the following day) when the invitation is reported.

sentence: They ___ us that the museum had closed early.
explanation: Tell somebody (that)... — 'told' needs the direct personal object 'us'; 'said' cannot take it.

sentence: She ___ that she would be waiting by the main entrance.
hint: say takes no personal object here
explanation: Say (that)... without a personal object; 'told that' is impossible without the object.

sentence: The witness ___ the police that he knew nothing.
explanation: Tell somebody that... — the personal object 'the police' requires told, not said.

sentence: He ___ to the reporters that the deal was off.
explanation: 'Said to the reporters that...' is correct; tell cannot be followed by 'to'.

sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.

sentence: She ___ that the storm had passed.
explanation: Without a personal object, use said (that)...; told requires an object.

sentence: 'Let's take a break,' she said. She ___ taking a break.
explanation: Suggestions are reported as suggest + -ing (or suggest that we take). Never 'suggested to take'.

sentence: 'I'm sorry I shouted at you,' he said. He ___ shouting at me.
explanation: Apologies take apologise for + -ing: apologised for shouting.

sentence: 'I'll definitely pay you back,' he said. He ___ to pay me back.
explanation: Promises take promise + to-infinitive: promised to pay me back.

sentence: 'Leave now or I'll call the police!' he shouted. He ___ to call the police.
explanation: A threatening conditional utterance is reported as threatened to do something.

sentence: 'You broke my phone!' she said to her brother. She ___ her brother of breaking her phone.
explanation: Accusations: accuse somebody of + -ing.

sentence: 'I'll carry those bags for you,' he said. He ___ to carry my bags.
explanation: Offers of help are reported as offered to do something.

sentence: 'No, I won't open the door,' he said. He ___ to open the door.
explanation: Refusals are reported with refuse + to-infinitive.

sentence: 'OK, I'll help you move house,' she said. She ___ to help me move house.
explanation: Agreement to a request is reported as agreed to do something.

sentence: 'It was me who ate the last biscuit,' the boy admitted. The boy ___ eating the last biscuit.
explanation: Admit takes a gerund (admit doing) or admit that + clause — never admit to do.

sentence: 'I didn't take your charger,' she insisted. She ___ taking my charger.
explanation: Denials are reported as deny + -ing: denied taking.

sentence: 'You should apply for the grant,' he told me. He ___ me to apply for the grant.
explanation: Advice is reported as advise + object + to-infinitive.

sentence: 'Don't forget your tickets,' she said to us. She ___ us to take our tickets.
explanation: 'Don't forget' maps onto remind + object + to-infinitive.

sentence: 'Would you like to stay for dinner?' they asked. They ___ me to stay for dinner.
explanation: Offers of this kind are reported as invited somebody to do something.

sentence: 'Well done, you've passed!' the examiner said. The examiner ___ me on passing.
explanation: Congratulations: congratulate somebody on + -ing.

sentence: 'Watch out for the ice on the road,' she said. She ___ us about the icy road.
explanation: Warnings about a danger: warn somebody about something (or warn sb to do).

sentence: 'The delay is your fault,' the manager said to her. The manager ___ her for the delay.
explanation: Blame takes the pattern blame somebody for something.

sentence: 'I really must have that report by five,' the editor said. The editor ___ on having the report by five.
explanation: Insisting on a demand: insist on + -ing (or insist that + clause).

sentence: 'Thank you for delivering it so quickly,' she said. She ___ me for delivering it so quickly.
explanation: Thanks are reported as thank somebody for + -ing.

sentence: 'You really ought to try the tasting menu,' the waiter said. The waiter ___ trying the tasting menu.
explanation: Recommend takes a gerund (recommend doing) when there is no object.

sentence: She ___ on seeing the manager immediately.
explanation: Only 'insist' takes on + -ing; suggest and offer take bare -ing/to-infinitive respectively.

sentence: He ___ me of leaking the story to the press.
explanation: Accuse somebody of + -ing. Blame uses 'for', thank and congratulate use different prepositions.

sentence: They ___ for arriving so late.
explanation: Apologise for + -ing; the other verbs do not take 'for + -ing' in this pattern.

sentence: The colonel ___ his soldiers to advance at dawn.
explanation: Order + object + to-infinitive reports a command; suggest and hope do not take object + infinitive.

sentence: The hijackers ___ to blow up the plane unless their demands were met.
explanation: A declared harmful action is reported as threatened to do something.

sentence: She ___ me not to worry about the deadline.
hint: tell sb not to do sth
explanation: Only 'tell' takes a personal object + not to + infinitive; 'said me not to' is impossible.

sentence: He ___ me his car for the weekend.
explanation: Offer takes the double-object pattern (offer somebody something); the others do not.

sentence: They ___ breaking the window, but nobody believed them.
explanation: Deny + -ing reports a rejection of the accusation; 'but nobody believed them' confirms the meaning.

sentence: "I will call you tomorrow." — She said she ___ me the next day.
explanation: Backshift: 'will call' becomes 'would call'.

sentence: "Where do you live?" — He asked me where I ___.
explanation: Statement order + backshift: 'where I lived'.

sentence: "Do not touch the wire!" — She warned me ___ the wire.
explanation: 'Warn somebody not to do' — 'not' comes before 'to'.

sentence: "Have you finished?" — She asked ___ finished.
explanation: 'Whether/if' + statement order + 'had' for the present perfect.

sentence: "I saw him yesterday." — He said he ___ him the day before.
explanation: Backshift one step: saw → had seen; yesterday → the day before.

sentence: "We are leaving now." — They said they ___ then.
explanation: 'Are leaving' → 'were leaving'; now → then.

sentence: "Can you help me?" — She asked ___ help her.
explanation: 'Can' backshifts to 'could'; statement order after 'if'.

sentence: "You broke my phone!" — She accused me ___ her phone.
explanation: 'Accuse somebody of doing something'.

sentence: "It was your fault." — They blamed me ___ the accident.
explanation: 'Blame somebody for something'.

sentence: "Congratulations!" — She ___ me on passing the exam.
explanation: 'Congratulate somebody on something' reports congratulations.

sentence: "I am sorry I am late." — He ___ for being late.
explanation: 'Apologise for doing something' reports an apology.

sentence: "Would you like a drink?" — He ___ me a drink.
explanation: 'Offer somebody something' reports "Would you like …?"

sentence: 'I'm looking for a flat near the hospital,' she explained. She explained that she ___ for a flat near the hospital.
explanation: Present continuous becomes past continuous in reported speech: was looking.

sentence: 'We'll be arriving on the red-eye,' they said. They said they ___ on the red-eye.
explanation: 'Will be arriving' backshifts to 'would be arriving'.

sentence: 'Don't touch the thermostat,' the technician warned us. The technician warned us ___ the thermostat.
explanation: Negative commands are reported with 'warned + object + not to + infinitive'.

sentence: 'Have you seen my reading glasses?' he asked. He asked ___ his reading glasses.
explanation: 'If/whether' reports a yes/no question; the tense backshifts to past perfect.

sentence: 'You should get a second opinion,' the doctor said. The doctor ___ a second opinion.
explanation: 'Advise' is the reporting verb that takes object + to-infinitive; suggest and offer do not.

sentence: 'I'm sorry I forgot the meeting,' she said. She ___ forgetting the meeting.
explanation: An apology is reported with 'apologised for + gerund'.

sentence: 'Let's walk to the launch instead of driving,' he said. He ___ to the launch instead of driving.
explanation: 'Suggest' takes a gerund, never a to-infinitive.

sentence: 'I'll pay for the damage,' he said. He ___ pay for the damage.
explanation: 'I'll pay' as a voluntary act is reported with 'offered to pay'.

sentence: 'When does the library open?' she asked. She asked ___ the library opened.
explanation: The original question word 'when' is kept in the reported clause.

sentence: 'It was your team that missed the deadline,' the director told us. The director ___ missing the deadline.
explanation: 'Blame somebody for something' is the correct pattern; 'accuse' takes 'of'.

sentence: 'Please don't leave until the lights are off,' the caretaker begged us. The caretaker begged ___ until the lights were off.
explanation: Begging somebody not to do something uses object + not to + infinitive.

sentence: 'I've already spoken to the insurers,' he reminded me. He reminded me that he ___ spoken to the insurers.
explanation: Present perfect backshifts to past perfect: had already spoken.
